prompt: Complete StepLogger.run so it logs its steps in order and uses a finally block to guarantee that "cleanup" is always logged, even when the method throws.
explanation: A finally block runs no matter how the try block exits: normal completion, a return, or an exception flying out of the method. That makes finally the right place for cleanup work that must never be skipped. Note that the exception is not caught here -- it propagates to the caller, but only after the finally block has run.
hints: Append "start" before the try block, then do the work inside try.
Inside try: if explode, add "work-failed" and throw new RuntimeException(...); otherwise add "work-done".
Put log.add("cleanup") in a finally block -- it runs even while the exception is propagating out.
